questions.title: Can the research substrate itself evolve?
questions.description: With model, budget, Lean toolchain, verifier, provenance boundary, and holdout tasks fixed, can controlled experiments on training-task traces select substrate choices that transfer to unseen tasks without increasing stale or invalid inheritance?

links.why: establishes formal proof as the first setting and exposes the need for repeated, inspectable action
shows that local tools and runtime state are part of the mathematical environment
collaborative scale exposes the gap between local activity and reusable shared state
verification, verdicts, and admission require an explicit evidence boundary
unfinished work needs structured objects before it can be safely inherited
persistent external state turns inheritance into a causal question
retrieval, derived views, and admission must remain distinct
runtime and cohort boundaries affect what a substrate can preserve
replaceability has levels and contracts rather than one binary property
evolution must preserve distinctions between evidence types
trace interpretation is needed to decide which substrate changes are worth testing

questions.title: What makes a local feedback loop trustworthy?
questions.description: Can a mathematical agent inspect the exact local state produced by an action, test the relevant consequence, and preserve the result as evidence about that action?

links.why: repeated proof attempts make action-to-feedback choices observable
Lean-aware probes make local state and diagnostics inspectable
evidence categories limit what local feedback can support

questions.title: How should unfinished mathematical work be represented?
questions.description: Which distinctions matter for continuation: active routes, valid certificates, unresolved obligations, failed branches, or the provenance of a claim?

links.why: swarm-scale traces expose many forms of incomplete and repeated work
judging separates candidate activity from admitted mathematical state
structured unfinished state is the direct representation experiment
unfinished state must remain distinct when it is persisted
ledger and derived views need to preserve provisional status

questions.title: When does persistent state become inherited research rather than a larger context window?
questions.description: Can a later agent inherit a versioned state, understand what is provisional, and make a new contribution without silently treating retrieval as proof?

links.why: shared activity does not by itself produce a state that a later agent can inherit
receipts and verdicts determine what may be admitted
unfinished objects need explicit status before inheritance
versioned external state makes causal inheritance measurable
canonical ledger and derived views separate access from admission
runtime boundaries affect how inherited state is interpreted

questions.title: What does replaceability require?
questions.description: Can an agent, maintainer, verifier, or runtime component be replaced at a stated semantic-contract level without invalidating the evidence?

links.why: mutable tool state is an early replacement boundary
persistent state must survive changes in the surrounding runtime
runtime lifecycle and cohort interfaces make replacement explicit
architectural force and information rights constrain replacement claims
replacement levels and mutable dependencies can be compared directly

questions.title: How can a research system learn from failures without flattening evidence?
questions.description: How should a research system record failures that change its direction while preserving differences between code, tests, computed results, formal proof, and open conjecture?

links.why: large-scale activity creates failure patterns that need interpretation
verdicts and receipts expose the difference between activity and evidence
a ledger can preserve revisions without rewriting prior state
evidence categories keep unlike outcomes distinct
trace analysis connects negative observations to changed questions
the atlas itself is an experiment in preserving research interpretation

questions.title: What should remain after a shared experience ends?
questions.description: What can remain returnable, interpretable, and alive after an immediate shared experience ends?

links.why: oncewhere carries the personal question of persistence and return into a creative medium
